AW-STUDY-0034 · Figure study

Low-Poly Figure Fidelity

The kids and the dog in Daddy's memory places were stacks of balls, boxes and tubes. Here they are rebuilt as a few smooth, skinned surfaces with real cloth, hair and fur, still low poly, so the storybook light and the pixel pass have shapes to work with. Each stage shows before on the left and after on the right, under the same light. Drag to turn them.

What changed, in numbers

FigureTrianglesSeparate piecesMaterialsCloth, hair and fur surfacesSmooth, welded normalsThin parts for skin glowBends at joints

Why the shaders can now do their job

One surface, not a pile

Each figure is a handful of lofted surfaces: rings along a path, like a sculptor's armature. Where the old kid had 30 separate lumps that each lit like a ball, the light now rolls across one body, so the rim and the soft wrap light read as a form.

Normals that keep a little facet

Normals are welded across seams and blended back towards the flat faces by a set amount per part (hair more, skin less). It still reads as low poly, but the shading has gradients for the pixel pass to dither instead of noise.

UVs in metres

Every surface has UVs measured in metres, so a stripe is 5 cm wide on a shirt, a sock or a sleeve. That gives real materials: a knit bump on cotton, a twill on denim, strands in the hair, fur on bub, rubber on soles.

Thin parts glow

Each vertex knows how thin the body is there. Ears, noses, fingers and bub's ears let the sun through when it is behind them: turn on "Sun behind" to see it.

Skinned, so joints close

The bodies are skinned to bones, with joints blended over two rings, so elbows and knees bend without gaps. The girl keeps her real walk, sit and reach clips; young Daddy and bub keep the poses the school jump drives.

Materials named for what they are

"white t-shirt", "red shorts", "blond mop", "black lab coat": one material each, which is how the game reads shading roles, and how a later pass can swap a whole look.

Verdict

  • It works, and it stays cheap. Each figure is a few thousand triangles and draws in a handful of calls, fine for a phone.
  • The look is ready for the light. With the same storybook light on both, the rebuilt figures show rim, sheen and glowing ears; the old ones only show their seams.
  • The games pick it up for free. The school jump and the basement use the same functions as before (makeYoungDaddy, makeBlackLab, loadGraceKid), so their next build gets these figures.
  • Next: a Midjourney turnaround of young Daddy, bub and the girl when the Mac is up, then tune each against it from all four sides.
